knowledge.text: The current intervention changes only principle 7 (the locate/acquire search rule): while the required object has not been acquired, every `go to` should advance to a not-yet-arrived-at instance, the current location should never be re-selected, rotating among already-checked instances of different types is itself a stall, and coverage should keep widening until the object is found. In the three current pairs whose object required a widened search, the Candidate advanced to a previously unarrived instance that held the object while the un-edited Parent kept re-entering locations it had already observed: val:0007 ('clean some butterknife and put it in drawer') — the Candidate worked through drawers 3-7 and then took butterknife 2 from the previously-unarrived countertop 4 (Q7:38, Q7:39) and finished in 43 steps, whereas the Parent cycled countertop 1 / countertop 2 / drawer 1 / drawer 2 / cabinet 1 (P7:1, P7:2, P7:4, P7:8, P7:37) and ended at the 50-step limit (P7:50) without ever selecting countertop 3 or countertop 4; val:0008 ('put a clean soapbar in cabinet') — the Candidate reached the untried open surface shelf 1 early (Q8:8, Q8:9), while the Parent re-entered countertop 1 / cabinet 1 / cabinet 2 / sinkbasin 1 many times before finally reaching shelf 1 (P8:23, P8:24); both succeeded, 13 vs 28 steps; val:0010 ('cool some apple and put it in microwave') — the Candidate moved directly to the previously-unarrived diningtable 1 and took apple 1 (Q10:3, Q10:4), while the Parent returned to countertop 1 / countertop 2 / fridge 1 before reaching diningtable 1 (P10:12, P10:13); both succeeded, 9 vs 18 steps. This Parent-failure/Candidate-success rescue plus two large success-preserving step reductions are consistent with the advance-to-new-instance requirement, but the clause constrains which destinations to avoid rather than which location type to try first, and the Actor sees only the current observation plus the last two pre-action observation/action pairs, so the whole-task differences are not uniquely attributable to the rewrite.

The principle-7 rewrite produced no observed change in these current pairs where the goal object was reached without prolonged search: val:0001 (examine bowl with desklamp), val:0002 (examine pillow with desklamp), val:0003 (put some mug on sidetable), val:0004 (put a mug in sidetable), val:0006 (put a clean butterknife in drawer) and val:0009 (put a clean soapbar in toilet) had identical Parent and Candidate action sequences and equal step counts (4/4, 5/5, 4/4, 4/4, 8/8, 6/6), with both sides succeeding. val:0006 still involved a short search — both sides went countertop 1 then countertop 2, took butterknife 1, cleaned it at sinkbasin 1, opened drawer 1 and delivered (P6:1-P6:8 / Q6:1-Q6:8) — so in these pairs the rewrite added no detour, no alternative route when the first new instance already held the object, and no extra post-acquisition search. This was not true of every short-search pair, however: val:0005 was also resolved without prolonged search, yet the Candidate reached pencil 1 in drawer 1 (Q5:4) and finished in 6 steps (Q5:6), while the Parent opened cabinet 1 and took pencil 3 from shelf 1 (P5:5) and finished in 7 steps (P5:7), so here the two sides followed different routes (a one-step difference) despite the short search.

The rewritten anti-revisit requirement was not sufficient to remove returns to already-observed locations within the same run: in val:0007 the Candidate repeatedly returned to countertop 1 (Q7:7, Q7:14, Q7:20, Q7:26, Q7:33) and to countertop 2 (first reached at Q7:2, then returned to at Q7:15, Q7:21, Q7:29, Q7:34) and re-checked drawers 1-6 (Q7:27, Q7:28, Q7:31, Q7:32, Q7:35, Q7:36) before finally advancing to the new countertop 4 (Q7:38); likewise, after drawers 1 and 2 had been observed without the object (Q7:4, Q7:6), the Candidate continued to drawer 3 (Q7:8) instead of switching to the still-untried countertop instances. Because the Actor keeps no persistent notes and can see only the current observation, the admissible actions and the last two pre-action observation/action pairs, these revisits are at least partly outside its visible history, so whether the rule was disregarded or was simply untrackable with that short window cannot be separated; the evidence shows the rule alone did not prevent short cycling, not that it was ineffective, since the Candidate still reached the object-bearing new instance and succeeded.

Across the ten current pairs the Candidate never did worse than the Parent: six pairs were identical (val:0001, val:0002, val:0003, val:0004, val:0006, val:0009) and four used fewer Candidate steps (val:0005 6 vs 7; val:0007 43 vs Parent step-limit 50; val:0008 13 vs 28; val:0010 9 vs 18), with no Parent-success/Candidate-failure regression. The effect was not uniform, however: on val:0005 ('put some pencil on desk'), a pair both sides completed, the only difference is a one-step local route choice — the Candidate opened the untried drawer 1 and took pencil 1 (Q5:2, Q5:3, Q5:4), while the Parent opened cabinet 1 (P5:2, P5:3) and then took pencil 3 from shelf 1 (P5:5) — so large or consistently attributable savings are not established, and only the three search-heavy pairs show large paired differences.
